name: Lithuanian University of Health Sciences
summary: Health-sciences university in Kaunas with 20 programmes in English, from Medicine and Pharmacy to seven bachelor's.

ib.text: Entrance test (interview plus biology and chemistry questions) unless you hold IB HL 5 in both Biology and Chemistry; biology and chemistry must be on your transcript. English at B1 or an LSMU English test.

programmes.name: Medicine
programmes.about: Six-year integrated degree producing medical doctors eligible for residency, combining medical science, clinical practice and research fundamentals on a problem-based curriculum.
programmes.overview: The first year covers anatomy, histology, genetics, physics and chemistry, followed by systems-based modules on reproduction and inheritance, neuroscience, immune response and infection, respiration and circulation, metabolism and locomotion, and the fundamentals of preclinical study. Years four to six are clinical modules and clinical practice. Teaching is problem-based, solving clinical cases in small groups of up to ten, with simulation equipment for practical skills and placements at the Baltic region's largest clinical hospital and other accredited hospitals across Lithuania. Research basics run through the curriculum and Erasmus+ exchanges are possible. Graduates qualify as medical doctors.

programmes.name: Odontology
programmes.about: Five-year integrated degree for dentists, combining biomedical sciences, pre-clinical training and supervised clinical practice to European standards.
programmes.overview: Foundation sciences such as anatomy, histology and embryology, biochemistry and physiology fill the first two years, then clinical specialities follow: cariology, endodontics, oral and maxillofacial surgery, orthodontics, periodontology and oral mucosal disease, prosthetic dentistry and paediatric dentistry, each with clinical practice. Teaching is problem-based, with simulation facilities and clinical training in groups of up to ten at the region's largest hospital system. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates can practise as dentists, go into residency or PhD programmes, or work in research and public health.

programmes.name: Pharmacy
programmes.about: Five-year integrated degree in drug development, pharmaceutical sciences and patient care, with practical training in public and hospital pharmacies.
programmes.overview: The first two years build biology, mathematics, physics, anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology, then pharmaceutical sciences: organic and analytical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmaceutical chemistry and technology, pharmacology, toxicology, clinical pharmacy and pharmacotherapy, pharmaceutical care, biotechnology and biopharmaceutics. Teaching is problem-based, in renovated laboratories with simulation equipment, and practical training takes place in public and hospital pharmacies. Erasmus+ exchanges for a semester or a year are possible. Graduates qualify as pharmacists.

programmes.name: Veterinary Medicine
programmes.about: Six-year integrated degree for veterinary surgeons, with theory, clinical practice and research on diagnosing, treating and preventing animal disease.
programmes.overview: Years one and two cover anatomy, histology, embryology and animal physiology, with husbandry, welfare, cell biology, microbiology and genetics. Years three and four add propaedeutics, pharmacology, pathology, toxicology, parasitology, immunology and epidemiology, and the last two years turn to diagnostic imaging, surgery on large and small animals, internal diseases, obstetrics, forensic medicine and food hygiene. Teaching combines theory, clinical practice and research in laboratories with simulation equipment, in clinical groups of up to ten. Graduates work in state food and veterinary services or private practice, or continue to a PhD or residency.

programmes.name: Nursing
programmes.credential: BSc in Health Sciences, General Practice Nurse
programmes.about: Trains nurses who understand nursing theory and methods and can assess the needs of healthy and chronically ill people, leading to a bachelor's degree and nursing qualification.
programmes.overview: Over four years you move from humanitarian-social and biomedical sciences, healthcare fundamentals and nursing techniques to nursing theory and introductory clinical subjects, then adult nursing, pedagogy, nursing administration and research methods, and finally specialised and geriatric nursing with final clinical examinations and a thesis defence. Teaching is problem-based, with simulation equipment, small clinical groups and placements at the region's largest hospital in departments such as oncology, neurology and interventional radiology. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work as general practice nurses at all levels of care or continue to a master's.

programmes.name: Occupational Therapy
programmes.credential: BSc in Health Sciences, Occupational Therapist
programmes.about: Trains occupational therapists: analysing a person's occupational performance, setting therapy goals, with research basics and practical skills.
programmes.overview: Year one combines philosophy, ethics, psychology, anatomy, cytology, genetics and first aid with occupational therapy theory and models and first practice. Later years cover occupational therapy for older people, physiology, pathology, biomechanics and rehabilitation, then mental health and activity disorders, community-based therapy, healthcare system management, research methodology and a bachelor's thesis. Practice is extensive, with more than a thousand hours in real settings, in small groups and taught by practising occupational therapists. Graduates work in hospitals, rehabilitation institutions, nursing homes and wellness services, or continue to master's and doctoral study.

programmes.name: Physiotherapy
programmes.about: Science-based study of movement therapy: assessing a patient's functional state and treating injury and illness through movement and physical interventions.
programmes.overview: The first year covers anatomy, physiology, cytology, genetics, psychology and the principles of physiotherapy, then biochemistry, biomechanics, pharmacology and methods of physiotherapy. Third-year topics include rehabilitation after nervous diseases, internal medicine, motor control, massage, musculoskeletal disorders and aquatic physiotherapy, and year four adds geriatrics, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology applications, research methods and a final examination. Over 1,200 hours of clinical practice take place in hospitals, family medicine centres and rehabilitation facilities. Graduates work in hospitals, clinics, rehabilitation, sports organisations and private practice, or continue to a master's.

programmes.name: Oral Hygiene
programmes.credential: BSc in Health Sciences, Dental Hygienist
programmes.about: Educates dental hygienists to EU-recognised requirements, with the right to provide oral health care and a focus on science and practice of oral health.
programmes.overview: Early years cover natural sciences, human anatomy, physiology, communication psychology, oral health and personal hygiene, ethics and ergonomics, with a phantom course in professional dental hygiene. Later years add professional dental hygiene, cariology, periodontology, oral surgery with pain control, pharmacology, radiology and prevention, then paediatric dentistry, oral care for older people and orthodontic patients, and an introduction to prosthetic dentistry, each with clinical practice. Teaching is problem-based, with simulation equipment, small clinical groups and Erasmus+ exchange. Graduates advise patients on prevention, run oral health promotion programmes and practise in public or private institutions.

programmes.name: Medical and Veterinary Genetics
programmes.credential: BSc in Life Sciences, Biomedical Technologist
programmes.about: Biological and pathological processes in humans and animals, with practical training in cytogenetics, molecular genetics and biochemical analysis for diagnostic and research laboratories.
programmes.overview: Human and animal physiology and basic genetics start the degree, followed by general and molecular pathology, molecular biology, biostatistics, immunology and plant genetics, then veterinary genetics, medical genetics, analytical chemistry and bioinformatics. A bachelor thesis runs through the last two years with professional practice in year four. Teaching is problem-based, with work in renovated laboratories and Erasmus+ exchange possible. Graduates work in diagnostic and research laboratories, healthcare and veterinary settings, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and food safety sectors, and environmental protection, or continue to a master's or PhD.

programmes.name: Medical and Veterinary Biochemistry
programmes.credential: BSc in Life Sciences, Biomedical Technologist
programmes.about: Trains biochemists for research in environmental monitoring, laboratory diagnostics and analysis of food and biopharmaceutical products.
programmes.overview: Year one lays foundations in biology, genetics, physics, general, organic and bioorganic chemistry, mathematics and anatomy. Years two and three cover biochemistry, physiology, microbiology, pathology, histology, molecular biology, biotechnology and genetic engineering, laboratory haematology, immunology, bioinformatics and diagnostic biochemistry, and the last year is professional practice and a final thesis. Teaching is problem-based, in renovated laboratories with Erasmus+ exchange possible. Graduates work in biochemical laboratories and private companies on disease diagnostics, environmental monitoring and food analysis, or continue to graduate programmes in laboratory diagnostics and natural sciences.

programmes.name: Health Psychology
programmes.about: Health psychology with a foundation of theory and practical skills on personal and public health, healthcare systems and promoting health and well-being.
programmes.overview: Year one starts with introduction to psychology, communication, neurophysiology, statistics and human ecology, then health, developmental and cognitive psychology with quantitative and qualitative research methods. Later you study clinical, social and educational psychology, crisis and disaster psychology, psychological assessment, psychiatry and health care systems, and finally counselling, work and organisational and rehabilitation psychology, behavioural medicine and health policy, ending with a bachelor's thesis. Coursework, practice and Erasmus+ exchange are part of the study. Graduates work as assistant psychologists, research or HR assistants in health, social, educational and organisational settings, or continue to a master's.

notes: English-taught places are fee-paying for everyone; the state-funded route through LAMA BPO is for Lithuanian-language studies. An EU/EEA citizen pays the same fee as others but a €1,500 deposit instead of a larger one.
Application fee is €150 after a free first review within 72 hours; once you have an offer, a €250 registration fee follows. Waiting-list places are reviewed each month.
Medicine, Odontology, Pharmacy and Veterinary Medicine fees rise in years 4 to 6; the amounts on the tuition fees page are for 2026/27.
